title: QR by modified Gram-Schmidt
prompt:
Write `mgs_qr(A)`: the thin QR decomposition of `A` (shape (m, n), m ≥ n, independent columns) by **modified** Gram–Schmidt. Return `Q` (m, n) with orthonormal columns and `R` (n, n), upper triangular with a positive diagonal, such that `A = Q @ R`.

Modified Gram–Schmidt normalizes one column at a time and immediately removes its direction from **all the remaining columns**, so later projections use the already-cleaned columns. Loops over columns are fine. Don't use `np.linalg.qr`: you'll compare against it afterwards.
hints: Column j of Q is column j of A with its components along q₀, …, q₍ⱼ₋₁₎ removed, then scaled to length 1. R records the amounts you removed and the lengths you divided by.

Work on a copy V of A. At step j: R[j, j] = ‖V[:, j]‖ and Q[:, j] = V[:, j] / R[j, j]. Then, for all the later columns at once, R[j, j+1:] = Q[:, j] @ V[:, j+1:] and V[:, j+1:] -= outer(Q[:, j], R[j, j+1:]). The classical version computes every projection from the original A, which is equal on paper but loses orthogonality in floating point.

V = A.astype(float).copy(); Q = np.zeros_like(V); R = np.zeros((n, n)). For j in range(n): R[j, j] = np.linalg.norm(V[:, j]); Q[:, j] = V[:, j] / R[j, j]; R[j, j+1:] = Q[:, j] @ V[:, j+1:]; V[:, j+1:] -= np.outer(Q[:, j], R[j, j+1:]). Return Q, R.

misconceptions.classical-gram-schmidt: Classical Gram-Schmidt computes every projection from the original column. In floating point its Q can lose orthogonality completely when A is ill-conditioned; the modified version, and Householder QR, don't.
